info:
Nouns have no grammatical gender and do not inflect based on number or case.

Plurality can be marked with the suffix -들 (-deul), but is often omitted when unnecessary for clarity.

Korean uses particles after nouns to express grammatical roles and relationships:

이/가 (i/ga) marks the subject. 이 is used after consonants, 가 after vowels.

을/를 (eul/reul) marks the direct object. 을 follows consonants, 를 follows vowels.

에 (e) shows location or time (like “at” or “to”).

에서 (eseo) indicates the location of an action or starting point.

의 (ui) marks possession (like "'s" in English).

와/과, 하고, (이)랑 can indicate "and" or companionship depending on formality and structure.

There are no articles; definiteness and specificity are often conveyed through context or demonstrative words like 이 (this), 그 (that).

을/를 (eul/reul) marks the direct object. 을 follows consonants, 를 follows vowels.

에 (e) shows location or time (like “at” or “to”).

에서 (eseo) indicates the location of an action or starting point.

의 (ui) marks possession (like "'s" in English).

와/과, 하고, (이)랑 can indicate "and" or companionship depending on formality and structure.

There are no articles; definiteness and specificity are often conveyed through context or demonstrative words like 이 (this), 그 (that).
